subject: fitting a model with nimbleMCMC for matrix data

messages.author: 0f0ebbb5d52633f8
messages.subject: fitting a model with nimbleMCMC for matrix data
parts:
Dear Nimble users

I'm trying to fit a very simple model in nimble (see the code below)
library(agridat)
library(nimble)
library(coda)

data(cornelius.maize)
dat <- cornelius.maize
#env<-dat$env
#gen<-c(dat$gen)
#gen
yield<-dat$yield
Y<-matrix(c(yield),nrow=20,ncol=9)
yn<-t(Y)
mm<-mean(y)
#Y;Yn
nv<-nrow(yn);nv
ne<-ncol(yn);ne

sortR <- nimbleRcall(prototype   = function(x = double(1)) {},
                     Rfun       = "sort",
                     returnType = double(1))


mcode<-nimbleCode({
mu~dnorm(0,tau=0.000001)
for(i in 1:nv){alpha[i]~dnorm(0,tau=1/nv)}
for(j in 1:nv){beta[j]~dnorm(0,tau=1/ne)}
for(i in 1:nv){
  for(j in 1:ne){
    y[i,j]~dnorm(m[i,j],tau)
    m[i,j]<-mu+alpha[i]+beta[j]
  }
}
tau~dgamma(0.1,0.1)
})

mConts<-list(ne=ncol(yn),nv=nrow(yn))#,m.mu=mean(y)
mData<-list(y=matrix(c(yn),nrow=nrow(yn))

nimbleModel(code=mcode,data=mData)

mcmc <- nimbleMCMC(code=mcode,constants=mConts,data=mData,
niter=10000,nburnin=2500,
summary=TRUE, samples=FALSE,
monitors=c('mu','alpha','beta'))
mcmc.

The data used in the code is type matrix with 9 row and 20 columns. I've the model code in OpenBUGS and is correct. But when I've run nimbleMCMC in the summary I've obtained NA. I suspect that I didn't correctly define the data.  

For this reason, I'd like to ask if someone could help me?

Best regards
Marcin

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: fitting a model with nimbleMCMC for matrix data
parts:
Hi Marcin,

It looks like you are not setting up priors for all the elements of beta.
You have
for(j in 1:nv){beta[j]~dnorm(0,tau=1/ne)}

but I think you mean to have "for j in 1:ne".  The issue is that nimble can't initialize all the beta values because you don't have priors for all the elements. 
I'm surprised that code would work in BUGS.

Also, it's often a good idea to provide good initial values and not rely on simulating from the priors. 

-chris

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: fitting a model with nimbleMCMC for matrix data
parts:
hi Marcin,

Nimble requires that you provide brackets when using vectors, matrices, arrays (and commas indicating dimensionality for matrices and arrays).
We also often need explicit indexing. So, for example, in the lines of code where you define D, W, and inte, you'll need to add this information, e.g.,

    D[1:2,1:2]<-diag(lam[1:2])
    W[1:nv,1:2]<-U[1:nv,1:2]%*%D[1:2,1:2]
    inte[1:nv,1:ne]<-W[1:nv,1:2]%*%t(V[1:ne,1:2])

There might be more going on, but that is a good place to start.

-Chris
